name: Duelist
description:
You raise your blade in front of your face and then point it at the hulking figure across the battlefield. You give a challenging cry and begin striding toward it. It answers the cry and moves in your direction. The rest of the battle falls away around you - it's just you and your chosen opponent in this moment. As they rear back to make a brutal strike, you read the angle of their step and shift just to one side of the blow as it comes down. Quickly, you lash out at their arm twice with deft swipes, leaving a pair of gashes. Their cry and the movement of their shoulders tells you that another blow is coming, so you spin around their back as they swing toward you, and with a lunge your blade finds a gap in their armor. They fall to their knees and you quickly deliver the coup de grâce with efficiency. You flick the blood off your blade and scan the battlefield for your next worthy opponent.

A Duelist represents the height of formalized combat. The killing blow is trivial compared to the delicate dance of engagement that precedes it. It is an artful dance when done well, and none do it better than Duelists.

The Duelist mestiere is all about engagement. You have the most engagement dice and have access to the most engagement successes. With your Good Form ability, success in engagement generates MP that you can spend to execute special combat maneuvers that lower an opponent's Defense, allow you to make extra attacks or inflict Injury on your opponent. What for others might be a quick contest preceding a blow expands into a battle of its own in your hands, allowing you to gain advantages others have to use brute force or magic to achieve.

Many other mestieri only dabble in engagement or ignore it entirely. The Duelist exploits that weakness.

Play a Duelist if you want to:

  • Fight with precision and style, building momentum through disciplined engagement and spending it at the perfect moment.

  • Demand to be met as an equal, using composure and bearing to compel opponents to face you and you alone.

  • Read and outmaneuver your opponents, answering every attack with technique and timing rather than raw strength.

Questions to consider when making a Duelist:

  • Who trained them? Do they follow a particular school of swordsmanship, or have they developed their own style through years of experience?

  • What does good form mean to them personally—a source of pride, a survival skill, a kind of aesthetic devotion, or all three?

  • What first drew them to dueling? An affair of honor, the influence of a mentor, a need to prove themselves, or simply a love of the craft?

  • Do they carry that sense of honor into the rest of their life, or is the dueling ground the only place they hold themselves to a higher standard?

  • Have they ever lost a duel that truly mattered? What did it cost them, and what did it teach them?

novizio.description: You are experienced in the art of dueling and have a library of maneuvers at your disposal. You bring a personal code of honor to the battlefield.
novizio.engagementDiceNotes: Multiply this base allotment by your WITS score (for example, a WITS score of 3 means you have a total of 6d4). Recalculate as your WITS score changes.
novizio.baseMpNotes: You gain MP through your Good Form ability.
novizio.abilities: Demand Satisfaction, Good Form and choose one, ignoring its XP cost: Press Advantage, Quick Draw, or Lunge.
novizio.gratuiti: A set of formal clothing, soap, polish, a badge of heraldry, a pair of gloves.
